summary: El Segundo packs an extraordinary concentration of aerospace and defense headquarters — Raytheon, Boeing, Northrop Grumman, and Chevron's western U.S. hub all sit within its roughly 5.5 square miles of developed land, making this tiny coastal city one of the densest corporate job centers in Los Angeles County relative to its population of just 17,000. That employer density means a rare thing for Southern California: a genuine live-and-work town where changing companies doesn't necessarily mean changing your commute. The flat, grid-style street layout between LAX to the north and the Chevron refinery to the south gives the core a compact, walkable feel anchored by a traditional Main Street with independent restaurants and coffee shops, though the refinery and airport infrastructure create hard edges that fragment the city's geography. With a median home price above $1.5 million against a median household income around $149,000 — a price-to-income ratio over 10:1 — buying here demands substantial wealth beyond local salaries alone, while rents near $2,550 consume roughly 20% of that median income, a more manageable ratio. Daily highs averaging 73°F year-round with over nine hours of sunshine, plus direct beach access along a stretch of South Bay coastline, deliver reliably mild weather without the marine-layer gloom that blankets neighborhoods farther up the coast. El Segundo is essentially an aerospace company town that happens to have a beach — an unusual pairing that defines both its economic resilience and its ceiling on affordability.
